title: Chicago White Sox Trade Deadline Recap: Breaking Down All 4 Moves - NewsBreak
text:
By Neal Henninger ,
1 hours ago The Chicago White Sox trade deadline strategy was in full effect for 2026 as they looked to shore up their roster for a potential division title and playoff run. The organization did just that, making four trades to acquire players and fill needs across the roster. The team also set itself up for success beyond this season with controllable assets rather than rentals.
Luis Castillo, RHP Jul 10, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Seattle Mariners pitcher Luis Castillo (58) delivers a pitch during the second inning against Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Filling a need in the pitching rotation, Chicago traded for Seattle Mariners starting pitcher Luis Castillo. While not the pitcher most expected to be dealt by Seattle, Castillo brings much-needed high-stakes experience to a team with playoff aspirations. Despite having a full rotation before the trade, pitcher Erick Fedde now moves to the bullpen.
Currently slumping compared to previous seasons, Castillo has a 3-9 record and a 5.06 ERA through 17 games in 2026. The starter has logged 99.2 innings pitched, with 86 strikeouts, 32 walks, and a 1.39 WHIP. Looking at his career numbers, Chicago is hoping the change of scenery gets him back around his 3.65 average ERA and 1.19 WHIP.
Chicago sent three players to the Mariners, including relief pitcher Seranthony Domínguez . The team also shipped outfield depth piece Nolan Jones and catching prospect Boston Smith to Seattle. The highlight of the deal for the Mariners, Smith, was ranked as the 15th-best prospect in Chicago’s minor league system.
Huascar Brazobán, RHP Aug 2, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; New York Mets pitcher Huascar Brazoban (43) walks off the field after the top of the eighth inning against the Miami Marlins at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images While many fans expected Chicago to acquire a closer, they instead went with a setup man. Taking advantage of a New York Mets sell-off, the White Sox traded for reliever Huascar Brazobán. Arguably their most reliable setup option before being traded, Brazobán comes to a contending team with multiple years of arbitration control.
Brazobán joins Chicago in the middle of a career season with a 5-2 record and an impressive 2.56 ERA over 46 games. In those games, he has 8 holds over 52.2 innings with 49 strikeouts, 23 walks, and a 1.01 WHIP. The bullpen in Chicago currently has a 3.78 ERA and a 1.30 WHIP, two stats that Brazobán will improve upon if he keeps his current pace.
The return for Brazobán was two pitching prospects for the Mets, including pitcher Gabe Davis, who ranked 18th in the White Sox system. The second prospect headed to the Mets is Triple-A pitcher Zach Franklin, a fringe top-30 to top-50 prospect.
Brenton Doyle, OF Aug 4, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Chicago White Sox center fielder Brenton Doyle (7) works for the ball off the wall against the Boston Red Sox in the first inning at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Most likely to be viewed as the surprise of the White Sox trade deadline was the acquisition of outfielder Brenton Doyle. Chicago decided to add the former Gold Glover to improve defense and is a bounce-back candidate to regain his hitting prowess. Outfielder Everson Pereira was designated for assignment to make room.
Doyle will look to turn his season around in Chicago and recapture his form as he slugs through an injury-shortened season. Playing 45 games in 2026, he is batting .214 with five home runs, 12 RBI, and an OPS of .569. Now healthy, the White Sox hope Doyle returns to the player he was when he won back-to-back Gold Glove awards in 2023 and 2024. Acquiring him appears to be a long-term move, as he is under control with three arbitration years.
Colorado acquired the highest-ranked prospect Chicago dealt at the deadline, eighth-ranked Mason Adams. The Triple-A pitcher ranks as the 19th-top prospect for the Rockies. International prospect Carlos Vielma also went to Colorado in the deal, where he will continue to develop as a shortstop.
Joey Bart, C Aug 4, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Chicago White Sox catcher Joey Bart (25) walks to the bullpen before the start of the game against the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images After starting catcher Kyle Teel suffered an injury, the White Sox acquired catcher Joey Bart from the Atlanta Braves. Adding the former first-round draft pick caused Chicago to option catcher Edgar Quero to the minors, as he had options remaining, unlike fellow catcher Drew Romo.
Looking at the catching options with the absence of Teel, almost anything would be considered an upgrade at the position. Bart is batting .220 this season with four home runs, 13 runs batted in, and an OPS of .688. While not impressive stats, it’s an improvement over the batting averages of Romo (.183) and Quero (.130), respectively. Another addition consistent with the theme of team control, Bart comes with another year of arbitration in 2027 before reaching free agency in 2028.
One of the more low-key trades that happened at the deadline, this was a one-for-one player deal. The Braves acquired right-handed pitcher Duncan Davitt from Chicago. The pitching prospect was ranked around 28th in the system, depending on the evaluator. Davitt has seen time in the majors this season, making his debut in April, pitching a scoreless inning against the Kansas City Royals.
End Of My Chicago White Sox Trade Deadline Rant:
Many fans expected the White Sox to make several trades to help them keep their division lead and make the playoffs. The Chicago White Sox trade deadline moves were clearly not just for the 2026 season, as all players they acquired have team control beyond this season. The White Sox made four trades at the deadline and improved their roster, though the level of improvement is open for discussion.
Chicago White Sox Trade Deadline Overall Grade: B
